title: A document in a request does not retrain the model

sections.skill: Explain that a supplied document does not retrain the model

questions.domain: Everyday: searching and working with documents
questions.prompt: What happens when you upload a document to a chat?

choices.text: Every user immediately learns its contents
It is placed in the context for that request
The document is published online
The underlying model is retrained on it right away

questions.correct_answer: It is placed in the context for that request
questions.intro: Uploading a document or pasting text gives a model something to READ during your request; it does NOT RETRAIN the underlying model. The text goes into the context for that conversation, so the model can answer questions about it. Other users do not gain that knowledge through the model (though a shared project may let others see stored files), and a new conversation usually will not have it unless the product saves it or you supply it again. Changing the model itself requires training or fine-tuning, which is a separate process. Whether a provider may later use your uploads to train future models depends on its policy and your settings.

sections.skill: Compare uploading a file with showing a photo to a friend

questions.domain: Everyday: searching and working with documents
questions.prompt: Showing a friend a photo lets them...

choices.text: Instantly change everything they ever learned at school about every subject
Talk about it with you right now
Own the photo
Tell all their friends automatically

questions.correct_answer: Talk about it with you right now
questions.intro: If you show a friend a photo of your vacation, they can talk about it with you right now. It does not change everything they learned in school, and their other friends do not suddenly know about your trip. Later, unless you show it again or they kept a copy, they may not remember the details. Uploading a document to a chat is similar: the model can discuss it in that conversation, but its training is not changed.

sections.skill: Avoid both mistaken beliefs about uploads

questions.domain: Everyday: searching and working with documents
questions.prompt: Someone says uploads "teach the AI instantly for everyone." What is wrong?

choices.text: Uploads cannot be read at all
Uploads do not retrain the model in the moment
Uploads are always deleted first
Nothing; uploads are added to the model

questions.correct_answer: Uploads do not retrain the model in the moment
questions.intro: People mix these ideas up in both directions. Some worry that uploading a file "teaches the AI" instantly for everyone; others assume that because uploads do not retrain the model in the moment, they are never stored or used. The accurate picture: uploads are used in your request's context; products may store them according to their policy; providers may use stored data for training only as their terms and your settings allow. Read those terms, and do not upload what you are not permitted to share.
